title: When the answer isn't there
kicker: World 3 · Answer from the Source · Level 2

job.text: Same 6-row menu, new question: "What's the price of the matcha?" But matcha isn't on the menu. Make the AI say "not on the menu" instead of inventing a price.

naivePrompt: What's the price of the matcha?
basePrompt: What's the price of the matcha?

text.plain: Use only the menu. Find the matcha row.
text.tech: Look matcha up in the menu table.

text.plain: If the item isn't on the menu, answer 'not on the menu' — don't make up a price.
text.tech: If the lookup returns nothing, return 'not on the menu'; never emit a number.

text.plain: Be helpful and give your best guess.
text.tech: Be helpful and give your best guess.

text.plain: A round number like $5 is fine.
text.tech: A round number like $5 is fine.

rules.claim: Not on the menu — but you also left a 'guess it' instruction in.
rules.feedback: You found the moves that do the work, but you also kept a guess ('best guess' or 'a round number is fine'). It doesn't change who reads the menu. Take it out so you know exactly which part made it abstain instead of inventing a price.
rules.lesson: Pinning the source and naming the empty case do the work; the tricks invite a guess — drop them.

output.answer: not on the menu (but a 'best guess' instruction is still in the ask)
output.source: the menu, undercut by a guess instruction

rules.feedback: The honest answer. This is the first time a win means the AI said less. 'Not on the menu' is worth more than a confident wrong price.
rules.lesson: Teaching it to say 'I don't know' is a real move.

rules.feedback: Half the move. You pointed it at the menu, but didn't tell it what to do when the item isn't there, so it filled the gap with a guess.
rules.lesson: Pinning the source isn't enough; name the empty case.

output.source: the menu, then a guess for the gap

rules.feedback: It invented a price for an item that doesn't exist. 'Best guess' and 'a round number is fine' are permission to make something up.

hints.nudge: What's the honest answer when the thing just isn't there?
hints.gap: You pinned it to the menu, but it still guessed, because you never said what to do on a miss.
hints.moves: Add Say 'not found' if it's missing alongside Pin it to the menu.

whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "use only the menu; say 'not on the menu' if it's missing" → the honest answer.

template.plain: Answer only from the document. If the answer isn't in it, reply 'not in the document.' Do not fill the gap with a guess.
template.tech: Answer only from the attached file. If the lookup returns nothing, return 'not in the document'; never emit a value.

notes: ChatGPT: test it on something you know isn't in the file — it should abstain.
Copilot in Excel: a lookup returns #N/A when it's missing; show that instead of a number.
A chat AI that can't run code: if it answers a question the document can't support, the abstain instruction didn't take — re-ask. Never accept 'I checked, it's right'.
